lines.japanese: 「あのサイズじゃなあ？　そりゃあ惚れるよなあ？」
lines.english: “At that size? Yeah, I can see how you’d fall for her.”
“...Huh? Oh?! No!”

lines.japanese: 「うわあ、待って日和子さん！　言ってません！　俺、なんにも言ってません！」
lines.english: “Whoa, wait, Hiyoko! I didn't say it! I didn't say anything!”

lines.japanese: 「あー、でも千歳君とひよちゃんって意外とお似合いかもしれないね」
lines.english: “Oh, but you and Hiyo might make a surprisingly good match, Shuusuke.”

lines.japanese: 「あーもー、紀奈子さんまで、勘弁してくださいよ。ほら、日和子さんがオブラート貼りつけても隠しきれないほどに迷惑そうな顔してるじゃないですか。いや、それも失礼きわまる話だなオイ」
lines.english: “Oh, come on, even you, Kinako? Spare me. Look, Hiyoko looks so annoyed that no amount of sugarcoating could hide it. Actually, that's incredibly rude too, hey.”

lines.japanese: 「いいええ。光栄ですわー、ほーほほほ」
lines.english: “Nooo. I'm hooonored. Hohoho.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふ、よかったね千歳君。ひよちゃんも満更じゃないみたいだよ」
lines.english: “Hehe, good for you, Shuusuke. Looks like Hiyo isn't entirely against it either.”

lines.japanese: 「ええっ！　紀奈子さん、アナタにはあれが満更じゃない目に見えるんですか！」
lines.english: “What?! Kinako, do those look like the eyes of someone who isn't entirely against it?!”

lines.japanese: 「ふふん、しかし鷲介よ。俺にはおまえこそ満更じゃないように見えるがな」
lines.english: “Heh. But Shuusuke, you look like the one who isn't entirely against it to me.”

lines.japanese: 「え、ええー？」
lines.english: “Huh? Uh?”

lines.japanese: そう、かな。
lines.english: Do I?

lines.japanese: 「ああ……まあ……」
lines.english: “Oh... Well...”

lines.japanese: そりゃあ、べつに俺の方には迷惑がる理由なんてないし。
lines.english: I didn't exactly have any reason to be bothered.

lines.japanese: と、それをそのまま口にするのも面白くないと思い、俺はちょっと言葉を変えてみました。
lines.english: But simply saying that wouldn't be interesting, so I put it another way.

lines.japanese: 「だって俺、もともと作家・玉泉先生のファンだもん」
lines.english: “I'm already a fan of Ms. Tamaizumi's writing, after all.”

lines.japanese: 続けて玉泉先生に向かって。
lines.english: Then, turning to Ms. Tamaizumi:

lines.japanese: 「ねえ？　言いましたよね？　最新作、面白かったって！」
lines.english: “Right? I told you, didn't I? Your latest work was good!”

lines.japanese: 読んでないけど。
lines.english: I hadn't read it, though.
“R-right...”

lines.japanese: あ、照れた？
lines.english: Oh, is she embarrassed?

lines.japanese: 「それはどうも、ありがとうござ──」
lines.english: “Well, thank you ve—”

lines.japanese: 「千歳それ、マジで言ってんの？」
lines.english: “Chitose, are you serious?”
“Huh?”

lines.japanese: 不快げな声色の横槍が刺しこまれて、俺は我が耳を疑いました。
lines.english: The interruption came in an irritated voice. I couldn't believe my ears.

lines.japanese: 「最新作って、あのなんか暗いやつでしょ。おまえファンだっつーならさ、なおさら正直な感想を言ってやるべきなんじゃないの」
lines.english: “Her latest work is that gloomy thing, right? If you're a fan, all the more reason to tell her what you honestly think.”

lines.japanese: え、英里子さん？　いきなり何を言いだすんでしょう、このひとは。
lines.english: E-Eriko? What was she suddenly talking about?

lines.japanese: その口ぶりじゃまるで、面白いわけがないって言ってるみたいです。それって俺はいいけど、日和子さんに失礼じゃ──
lines.english: The way she said it made it sound like it couldn't possibly be any good. Never mind me, wasn't that rude to Hiyoko—

lines.japanese: ──ていうか、あれ？　むしろ日和子さんに言ってる？
lines.english: —Wait, huh? Was she actually saying it to Hiyoko?

lines.japanese: 日和子さんは頭こそ水平を保っていましたが、目だけは下を向いていました。
lines.english: Hiyoko kept her head level, but her eyes were lowered.

lines.japanese: ふたりのあいだに挟まれている紀奈子さんが、腰のあたりで両てのひらを英里子さんへ向けています。
lines.english: Between the two, Kinako held both palms toward Eriko around waist height.

lines.japanese: そういえば会が始まって以来、この三人の立ち位置はおおむね紀奈子さんがセンターを占めていた気がします。俺はマスターの表した「喧嘩友達」という婉曲表現を思いだしました。すると彼女は仲介役か。
lines.english: Come to think of it, Kinako had mostly stood in the center of these three since the party began. I remembered the boss's euphemism, “sparring partners.” So she was their mediator?

lines.japanese: 「え、えりちゃん、あんまり本人を前にしてそういう話は……」
lines.english: “E-Eri, maybe not that kind of talk in front of her...”

lines.japanese: 「なーんで。本人の前で言わなきゃ陰口ンなっちゃうでしょー」
lines.english: “Whyyy? If I don't say it in front of her, it's talking behind her back.”

lines.japanese: 日和子さんは、一同に背中を向ける格好となる位置の料理を選んで皿に盛っていました。
lines.english: Hiyoko was choosing food in a spot that required her to turn her back on us all, and serving it onto her plate.

lines.japanese: ──あれ？
lines.english: —Huh?

lines.japanese: でも日和子さんって、俺とかマスターには言いたいこと言える子なのに、英里子さんには頭が上がらないのでしょうか。
lines.english: Hiyoko could say whatever she liked to me or the boss. Was she unable to stand up to Eriko?

lines.japanese: ああ、それとも、内容が内容だけに自らは反論しにくいのかな。
lines.english: Or was it hard to argue herself, given the subject?

lines.japanese: だったら、こんな話を振っちゃった責任もあることだし、俺がさっさと流してしまわねばなりません。
lines.english: Then, since I was responsible for bringing it up, I needed to steer us past it quickly.

lines.japanese: 「そっかー、英里子さんには合わなかったのかー、俺はけっこー面白いと思ったんすけどねー」
lines.english: “Ohhh, so it wasn't for you, Eriko. I thought it was pretty good, though.”

lines.japanese: 「まあ、ひとの好みは十人十色ってことで、ねえ、いいじゃないすか。ははは」
lines.english: “Well, everyone's tastes are different, so that's fine, right? Hahaha.”

lines.japanese: 「じゃあ、千歳はあの眠くなる本のどこが良かったの。具体的に」
lines.english: “Then what did you like about that sleep-inducing book, Chitose? Specifically.”

lines.japanese: 「え……具体的に……？」
lines.english: “Huh... Specifically...?”

lines.japanese: なんて嫌な質問をしてくるんでしょう。
lines.english: What a nasty question to ask.

lines.japanese: 実はまだ読んでません──だなんて、五分前ならまだしも、いまとなってはとても言いだせる空気じゃありません。
lines.english: Actually, I haven't read it yet. Five minutes ago, maybe I could've said that. In this atmosphere, absolutely not.

lines.japanese: くそう、良かれと思って広げた嘘が、かえって自らを苦しめることになろうとは！
lines.english: Damn it, the lie I'd expanded with the best of intentions was coming back to torment me!

lines.japanese: 「千歳ぇー？」
lines.english: “Chitoseee?”

lines.japanese: 「あ、いや、理屈じゃなくてですね、なんていうかこう、全体の雰囲気がフィットしたわけでして、ええまあ、細かいことは作品論になりますから……こういう場では、ねえ、読んでないひとには退屈でしょうし……」
lines.english: “Oh, no, it's not a question of logic, you see. How should I put it? The overall mood just clicked with me. Well, the details would turn into literary criticism... In a setting like this, you know, it'd bore people who haven't read it...”

lines.japanese: 「えー、俺も聞きたいけどなー」
lines.english: “Oh, I'd like to hear it too.”

lines.japanese: くっ……カケルくんったら、事情を知っててなんて意地悪な！
lines.english: Ghh... Kakeru knew what was going on. How could he be so mean?!

lines.japanese: しかしそんな窮地を、意外な人物が救ってくれました。
lines.english: But an unexpected person rescued me from that predicament.

lines.japanese: 「いやだ。俺はそんな話はいやだ。ただちに素人ブルマ乱れ咲きの話がしたい」
lines.english: “No. I refuse. I refuse to discuss this. I demand that we proceed at once to the subject of amateurs in bloomers, blossoming everywhere.”

lines.japanese: 「そ、それだ！　ブルマー万歳！　ブルマー、それは男を惑わす永遠のロマン！」
lines.english: “Th-that's it! Long live bloomers! Bloomers—the eternal dream that leads all men astray!”

lines.japanese: 俺は道化精神にのっとり、さあ会衆よ我を見よとばかりに、いまこそ幻の珍獣ブルマニアデビルの皮を被りました。心で泣きながら。
lines.english: True to my jester's calling, I donned the hide of that legendary cryptid, the Bloomer-Maniac Devil, and all but cried: Behold me, congregation! All while weeping on the inside.

lines.japanese: 「き、聞いてくださいよマスター！　ブルマーと言えば、俺は裾を中に入れろ派なんですよ！」
lines.english: “L-listen, Master! When it comes to bloomers, I'm firmly in the tuck-the-hems-in camp!”

lines.japanese: 「ほう。真性だな」
lines.english: “Oh. The genuine article.”

lines.japanese: 「当ったりまえじゃないですかあ！　外に出すなんて豚に真珠──いや、もう豚っていうか豚以下のメスブタですよ！　そんな腐れブルマは屠殺場でまるまる肥えて死んでしまいますようにと星に願っちゃいますね！」
lines.english: “Obviously! Wearing them loose is pearls before swine—no, swine is too good for that. It's the work of a sow lower than any pig! I wish upon a star that every last pair of those rotten bloomers will grow fat and die in the slaughterhouse!”

lines.japanese: 「それから色！　色はやっぱり紺っすよ！」
lines.english: “And then there’s color! They’ve got to be navy blue!”

lines.japanese: 「ほう。いよいよだな」
lines.english: “Oh. Getting serious now.”

lines.japanese: 「だってほら、サッカーや柔道の例があるように、きっと日本人は青の似合う民族なんすよ。赤だの緑だのの亜種は、アメリア＝ブルマー女史の遺志を正しく世に伝えていないとさえ思えて慨嘆の念を禁じえませんね」
lines.english: “Look at soccer! Look at judo! Clearly the Japanese are a people born to wear blue. Red and green variants so utterly fail to communicate the true will of Amelia Bloomer to the world that I cannot restrain my lamentation.”

lines.japanese: 「わー、すごーい。語ってるー。こんなブルマー好きなひと初めて見たー」
lines.english: “Wow. Amazing. Listen to him go. I've never met anyone who loved bloomers this much.”

lines.japanese: 「てゆうか千歳キモい」
lines.english: “Actually, Chitose, you're creepy.”

lines.japanese: 「ふふん、キモくて結構ですよ喧嘩上等ですよ。こちとらそんな、ブルマのひとつも見せちゃくれないアイアンバージン共に媚びへつらう騎士道精神なんか、ブルマの毛玉ほども持ちあわせてないですからね、くくく」
lines.english: “Hmph. Gross and proud of it. Bring it on. I haven't got so much as a lint ball's worth of chivalry to waste flattering a pack of iron maidens who won't flash me a single pair of bloomers. Heh heh heh.”

lines.japanese: 俺は唇の横に親指と人差し指で輪を作って、空想煙草をくゆらせました。心で泣きながら。
lines.english: Making a ring with thumb and forefinger beside my lips, I puffed an imaginary cigarette. Crying inside.

lines.japanese: 「おー、みんな見るな見るなー。変態は相手すると喜ぶだけだぞー」
lines.english: “Hey, nobody look, nobody look. Paying attention to perverts only makes them happy.”

lines.japanese: 「大丈夫です。最初から一瞥たりともしてません」
lines.english: “Don't worry. I haven't spared him a glance from the start.”

lines.japanese: おおっ、ふたりのあいだに、裂けかけた溝を埋めるジョークの架け橋が！　すごい、俺すごい！　紀奈子さんも安堵の溜息だ！
lines.english: Ohhh, a bridge of jokes across the crack forming between them! Amazing. I'm amazing! Even Kinako sighed in relief!

lines.japanese: 調子付いた俺は、椅子にふんぞりかえってブルマーにかける果てなきドリームを語りつづけました。心で泣きながら。
lines.english: Emboldened, I sprawled back in my chair and continued holding forth on my boundless dreams of bloomers. All while weeping on the inside.

lines.japanese: 「あ～あ、残る余生はブルガリアでブルマン飲みながらブルドッグといっしょにブルマーを愛でていたいなあ。寝ても覚めてもブルマーブルマー。ああ、憧れのブルマーブルース」
lines.english: “Ah, what a life—to spend my twilight years in Bulgaria, sipping Blue Mountain coffee with a bulldog and gazing upon bloomers. Bloomers in my sleep, bloomers when I wake. Ah, the Bloomer Blues of my dreams.”

lines.japanese: 「いいんじゃないですか。誰も止めはしませんよ」
lines.english: “Fine, isn't it? Nobody's going to stop you.”

lines.japanese: 「うるさいメスブタ。俺と口を利きたければまずブルマーを穿け」
lines.english: “Shut up, sow. If you want to talk to me, put on bloomers first.”

lines.japanese: ぶるぶるぶるぶる……（怒りに身を震わせる日和子）
lines.english: Tremble, tremble, tremble, tremble... (Hiyoko shakes with anger.)

lines.japanese: ぶるぶるぶるぶる……（恐怖に身を竦ませる鷲介）
lines.english: Tremble, tremble, tremble, tremble... (Shuusuke shrinks with fear.)

lines.japanese: 「ああ、そうそう。これオフレコだけど、秋田県の男鹿半島一帯には、手桶と出刃包丁を提げた鬼が『ブルマはいねぇが！』などと奇声をあげながら家々を訪れるという微笑ましいフォークロアがあるらしいよ」
lines.english: “Oh, right. This is off the record, but apparently there's a charming bit of folklore around the Oga Peninsula in Akita. Masked demons carrying wooden pails and cleavers go from house to house shrieking, 'Any girls in bloomers here?'”

lines.japanese: 「ねえよ」
lines.english: “Nope.”

lines.japanese: 「よし。ならば鷲介、おまえがブルマゲ第一号になってみせろ」
lines.english: “Excellent. Then you, Shuusuke, shall become the world's first Bloomer Bogeyman.”

lines.japanese: 「それだ！」
lines.english: “That's it!”

lines.japanese: 「ぶるるる！　ブルマっ娘はいねーがぁぁぁ！」
lines.english: “Brrrrr! Any girls in bloomers heeeere?”

lines.japanese: 「はあ。いましたよ。さっき、あっちに」
lines.english: “Oh. There was one. Over there, earlier.”

lines.japanese: 「え、マジすか？　どっち？」
lines.english: “Huh, seriously? Which way?”

lines.japanese: 「あっちです。ずっとあっち。外に出て花水木通りを北に２００キロほど」
lines.english: “Over there. Way over there. Go outside, then north on Dogwood Street for about two hundred kilometers.”

lines.japanese: 「そのあと、突きあたりを上に折れて徒歩２年」
lines.english: “Then turn upward at the end and walk for two years.”

lines.japanese: 「ようし、近いな……」
lines.english: “All right, nice and close...”

lines.japanese: 「ごめん、みんな！　俺ちょっと急用ができたんで！　じゃ！」
lines.english: “Sorry, everyone! Something urgent's come up! Bye!”

lines.japanese: 俺は大袈裟に手を振って、とりあえず席を離れました。いったん下座へ消えて仕切りなおすとしましょう。
lines.english: Waving extravagantly, I left my seat for now. Time to disappear from center stage for a moment and regroup.

lines.japanese: 上げっぱなしじゃ持ちません。パーティーにチルアウト・タイムは不可欠です。
lines.english: You can't last if you keep the energy up all the time. A party needs chill-out time.

lines.japanese: 「ぶるまー、ぶるまー、ぶるるるーん！」
lines.english: “Bloomers, bloomers, brrrrr-oomers!”

lines.japanese: なんつって、こう、翼を広げて駆けだしたぼく。
lines.english: Or something like that. I spread my wings and ran.
